messages.subject: Fitting NGARCH in RStan
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to fit this special NGARCH stochastic volatility model using RStan, see this image

http://imgur.com/90BFyHJ

or if the image is not showing:


dR_t = (r + lambda * sqrt(h_t) - 0.5 * h_t) dt + sqrt(h_t) dW_1t

dh_t = omega * dt + (beta + alpha * (1 + gamma^2) - 1) * h_t * dt + 2 * gamma * alpha * h_t * dW_1t + sqrt(2) * alpha * h_t dW_2t


where,

- R is log-returns (observed)

- h is volatility (to be estimated)

- alpha, beta, gamma, omega, r, lambda are parameters (to be estimated)

- W1 and W2 are two independent Wiener processes


I have looked at the stochastic volatility examples in the repository, but I do not see how I should be able to fit my own model? I think, I am confused by the existance of two independent shocks and the fact that the volatility also enters in the mean model.


Best,

Masih

messages.author: 29ce8550baceaeb0
messages.subject: Re: Fitting NGARCH in RStan
parts:
Hi Masih - 

Another approach would be to convert the model into discrete time and estimate it directly. 

If you normalize the time period to 1 (so that your volatility measures will be interpreted 
as volatility over that time period), dt = 1 and dW ~ normal(0, 1). After a bit of re-arranging, 
it is a fairly simple model. The trick is coding the dW terms as latent variables which you assign
distributions. If you want to go to higher frequencies, you should appropriately scale the 
innovations. 

I've provided a worked example here. Please don't follow my bad example: save the model
file in its own .stan file. I've only included the model as a string so that you can run the entire 
script and it will work: 

https://gist.github.com/khakieconomics/cc085366707388936eb8f7d40ad7b5e7

The model seems to be able to recover known parameters _reasonably_ well, with the 
exception of alpha, beta and gamma. gamma in particular doesn't seem to be very strongly
identified. The model seems to be capable of recovering known volatility quite well. 

Cheers, 
Jim
